stations.name: What it covers
stations.meaning: Which hazard, which asset, which parts; what is left out
stations.paragraph: Convective wind on solar farms: thresholded logistic curves on a design-normalised demand ratio; axis from wind-pressure physics, all numeric parameters set by engineering judgment from PV wind-load and storm-resilience sources. It names 5 parts: Tracker structure, Racking structure, PV module attachment, Foundations (uplift) and Exposed SCADA and met station. Outside its scope: tornado and windborne debris (deferred to a separate pathway) and yearly and tail loss metrics (computed by the consumer, not the cell). Kinds of damage it does not include: cascade between racking or tracker failure and module detachment (no dependency rule).

stations.name: What breaks
stations.meaning: The parts of the plant the hazard damages, each with its own curve
stations.paragraph: For this hazard the solar farm is split into 5 parts: Tracker structure, Racking structure, PV module attachment, Foundations (uplift) and Exposed SCADA and met station. Parts of the plant's value with no curve yet: the other 36% of the reference physical base (parts not named by the cell) has no curve or value share; the cell says this is not an automatic zero.

stations.name: How damage is measured
stations.meaning: The hazard intensity on the x-axis and the shape of the curve
stations.paragraph: Damage is read against effective demand ratio R_eff = (V₃ₛ / V_design)² × demand multipliers. The curve is nothing below a threshold, then an S-shaped rise to a plateau (thresholded logistic). The input, in the catalogue's words: 3-second gust at array height (mph), 0 to 200 (warn or clamp), turned into a demand ratio: (gust / design gust) squared times stow and zone multipliers.

stations.name: Where the numbers come from
stations.meaning: The sources, what was taken from each, and how sure we are
stations.paragraph: 10 sources set this cell: Wind-pressure physics, pressure scales with speed squared, CPP, utility-scale PV wind-load paper, CPP, torsional instability of single-axis trackers and DOE/FEMP, severe-weather PV design guidance and 6 more. Of the 26 parameters, 1 is lab-tested (T2) and 25 are our judgment (T4). The sources were read from the workbook's Evidence_Params, Assumption_Register and Sources sheets, because this older cell keeps them there rather than in register files. 1 source ID in the tier table (WIND_PRESSURE_PHYSICS) matches no document in the workbook or dossier.

stations.name: What it is worth
stations.meaning: The share of the plant's value the curves cover
stations.paragraph: The damage ratio is a share of replacement value of the same part, as a share of the physical replaceable base (default shares are illustrative). The files state no plant-level dollar figure for this asset. Shares of the plant's physical value, as the cell states them: Tracker structure 8 %, Racking structure 6 %, PV module attachment 40 %, Foundations (uplift) 8 % and Exposed SCADA and met station 2 %.

stations.name: The audit
stations.meaning: The seven checks a curve passes before release
stations.paragraph: The adjustments — which selectors and conditioners change the curve — are written in the dossier; no seven-step audit table exists as a file. A site-condition adapter has not been written for this cell.

stations.name: The files
stations.meaning: The runtime file, the write-up and the workbook
stations.paragraph: The runtime file is the curve artifact with 5 curve records (model v1.0, docs r3). The write-up is strong_wind_solar_curve_derivation_dossier__model_v1_0__docs_r1.md. The workbook is damage_curve_records_model_v1_0_docs_r1_strong_wind_solar.xlsx. The cell folder holds 7 files, each with its SHA under Details.

stations.name: What it can output
stations.meaning: What a consumer may compute with this curve
stations.paragraph: It can give one convective wind event. A dollar scenario, yearly loss and PML, VaR and TVaR are available only under conditions the consumer (Hazard) checks. Annual metrics belong to the consumer; nothing here is an expected annual loss.

stations.name: How it was tested
stations.meaning: The known answers this build reproduced
stations.paragraph: The artifact declares no known-answer tests, so this build reproduced none. No validation record was found. No outside check has been made yet.

stations.meaning: Field reports of this damage, and who has read the entry
stations.paragraph: Not searched — nobody has looked for field reports yet. The catalogue entry has been read by an agent only (2026-10-19); no person has reviewed it yet.

assumptions.text: Generic v1.0 uses engineering-fit fragility curves on effective demand ratio, not claims-calibrated wind-speed DRs.
assumptions.trigger: Adopt when claims/forensic datasets provide wind-speed + loss anchors.

assumptions.text: Design gust speed default is 120 mph for illustrative example; production should use site-specific ASCE/project design documents.
Stow demand multipliers are directionally source-supported but numerically generic placeholders.
assumptions.trigger: Replace with tracker-specific wind tunnel/aeroelastic/SCADA evidence.

assumptions.text: Module attachment and racking curves can overlap; v1.0 flags dependency but does not implement a full cascade model.
assumptions.trigger: Implement dependency/cascade assembly in v1.1 if needed.

assumptions.text: Foundation uplift curve is highly site/foundation-specific and should be considered a generic structural-zone placeholder.
Tornado/debris/missile damage is out of v1.0 and should not be represented by simply extending straight-line gust speed.
assumptions.trigger: Create tornado × solar pathway if tornado source data is in scope.
